name: @skaile-ai/annotation-inbox
description: Annotation toolbar whose notes reach coding agents with SFC source locations: framework-free core, Nuxt module, Vite plugin, HTTP and MCP surface
//exports: Entries, and for each one who compiles it. `.` is the framework-free core, `./nuxt` the Nuxt module, `./vite`, `./inbox`, `./mcp`, `./server` and `./testing` are all loaded by Node or a test runner directly, and Node refuses to type-strip TypeScript under `node_modules`, so every one of them is built to `dist/` with declarations. `./mount` is raw source on purpose: the consumer's Vite is its compiler, and pre-bundling it would risk the `import.meta.env.DEV` dead-branch elimination that is what keeps the toolbar out of production builds. The Nuxt module's runtime (`modules/annotation-inbox/runtime/**`, plus the contract/inbox/principal files it imports) ships as source for the same reason — Nuxt and Nitro compile it; the built `dist/nuxt.mjs` locates it at `../modules/annotation-inbox`.
//scripts: `prepare` rather than `prepack`, because npm runs `prepare` for a git dependency after it is cloned, so a package installed straight from GitHub arrives with `dist/` built.
//peerDependencies: Everything the package imports from its host and must not bring a second copy of: `@nuxt/kit` in `src/nuxt.ts`, `searchForWorkspaceRoot` from `vite` in `vite.ts`, `vue` dynamically in `runtime/mount.ts`, `vitest` in `./testing`. All are optional, because a consumer that only wants the core, `./inbox`, `./server` or `./mcp` needs none of them; Nuxt consumers already have them.
//dependencies: `unstorage` is the store seam: the server half reads and writes only through it, so a host can mount a filesystem directory, a database or anything else with a driver without this package knowing which. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `zod` are the stdio MCP server in `./mcp`.
